newsitem.title: CANADA: Canbra Foods shares rise after deal fails.
newsitem.headline: Canbra Foods shares rise after deal fails.

text.p: Canbra Foods Ltd shares recovered C$2.50 a share on the Toronto Stock Exchange after Tuesday's announcement that its majority shareholder withdrew an offer to buy outstanding shares at C$22.63 each.
"In essence, it's a dead deal. It's business as usual. Hartford Securities still owns 53 percent of the shares," Canbra vice-president Keith Beerling told Reuters by phone.
One of the consents required by Hartford Securities, a wholly owned unit of Pocklington Financial (1996) Corp, for the financing necessary was not granted by Tuesday, he said.
Canbra shares reached C$17.50 at 1100 EST as 6,250 traded.

Canbra shares closed at C$15 on Tuesday. The canola crushing, processing and packaging firm's president last week told Reuters he expected share value to decline to C$14 each if Peter Pocklington's buyout plan did not materialize.

The company planned to operate at about 80 percent of its 1,000-tonne-a-day crush capacity leading up to the Christmas holiday and expected to scale production back unless profit margins improved, president Larry McNamara said last week.
Winnipeg Commodity Exchange January futures crush profit margin fell to -38.11 on Tuesday from -38.03 Monday on January Chicago Board of Trade soyoil and soymeal.
